source_text: Verum ut illi infensus Iovinianus arguitur, ita vobis comparatus absolvitur. Quando enim tibi tantum prudentium censura donabit, ut te cum Ioviniani merito componat? Ille quippe dixit boni esse necessitatem; tu, mali; ille ait per mysteria homines ab errore cohiberi; tu vero, nec per gratiam liberari; ille virginitatem Mariae partus conditione dissolvit; tu ipsam Mariam diabolo nascendi conditione transcribis; ille meliora bonis aequat, id est, integritatem connubio; tu vero commixtionem coniugii morbidam vocas, et castitatem foedissimae rei collatione depretias; nec gradum inter haec addis; sed genus omne commutas, non utique bono virginitatem, sed malo praeferens. Est autem vilitatis extremae, nisi teterrimo comparatum, placere non posse. Iam vero quid ille tale de Dei iniuriis, quale tu? Ille eius iudicii vigorem a benignitatis voluit parte confundere; tu a malignitatis; ille dicit apud eum bonos et optimos aequo honore fruituros; tu vero, bonos et impios, id est innocentes et diabolum, uno supplicio cruciandos; ille ergo Deum clementissimum vult videri; tu, iniquissimum; ille dicit mysteriis eius imbutos homines non posse peccare; tu vero ipsum Deum, et in mysteriis imbecillitate, et in praeceptis immoderatione, et in iudiciis immanitate peccare contendis. Cum itaque tanta disparatio sit inter te et Iovinianum, quanta coniunctio inter te et Manichaeum; tanto te tolerabilior Iovinianus probatur, quanto Ioviniano horridior Manichaeus.
pass_a_gloss: But as Jovinian is accused as hostile to him, so compared with you he is acquitted. For when will the censure of the prudent grant you so much, that it compose you with Jovinian's desert? For he said there is a necessity of good; you, of evil; he says humans are held back from error through mysteries; you however, that they are not even freed through grace; he dissolved Mary's virginity by the condition of birth; you transfer Mary herself to the devil by the condition of being born; he equates better things with goods, that is, integrity with wedlock; you however call the mingling of marriage diseased, and depreciate chastity by comparison with a most foul thing; nor do you add a step between these; but you change the whole genus, preferring virginity not indeed to a good but to an evil. But it is of extreme cheapness not to be able to please unless compared with the most foul. Now indeed what of such a kind did he concerning injuries of God, as you? He wanted to confuse the vigor of his judgment from the side of kindness; you from that of malignity; he says that with him the good and the best will enjoy equal honor; you however, that the good and the impious, that is the innocents and the devil, are to be tortured with one punishment; he therefore wants God to seem most clement; you, most unjust; he says humans imbued with his mysteries cannot sin; you however contend that God himself sins, both by weakness in mysteries, and by immoderation in precepts, and by monstrosity in judgments. Since therefore there is as great a disparity between you and Jovinian as a conjunction between you and Manichaeus; Jovinian is proved as much more tolerable than you as Manichaeus is more horrible than Jovinian.

pass_b_english: Yet although Jovinian is accused of hostility to Ambrose, he is acquitted when compared with you. When will the judgment of sensible people grant you enough credit to place you on the same level as Jovinian? He said there was a necessity for good; you, for evil. He said people were kept from error through the mysteries; you say they are not freed even through grace. He dissolved Mary’s virginity by the condition of childbirth; you transfer Mary herself to the devil by the condition of being born. He equates better things with good things—that is, virginity with marriage. You call marital union diseased and cheapen chastity by comparing it with something utterly foul. You do not insert a difference of degree between them; you change the whole category, preferring virginity not to a good but to an evil. It is the utmost cheapness to be pleasing only in comparison with something utterly disgusting.

Again, what did he do to insult God that resembles what you do? He wanted to weaken the force of God’s judgment on the side of kindness; you, on the side of malice. He says the good and the best will enjoy equal honor before God. You say the good and the impious—that is, the innocent and the devil—will be tormented by one punishment. He wants God to appear supremely merciful; you, supremely unjust. He says people initiated into God’s mysteries cannot sin. You contend that God himself sins: by weakness in the mysteries, by excess in his commands, and by cruelty in his judgments. Since the distance between you and Jovinian is as great as the closeness between you and Manichaeus, Jovinian is proved more tolerable than you to the same degree that Manichaeus is more dreadful than Jovinian.
